gap: No result ChatGPT got says, in one place, that the same "24 A" works three different ways on these chargers: EVDANCE's 14-30 has a top setting of 24 A (settings 10/16/20/24 A), Tesla's Mobile Connector is held to 24 A by its $45 Gen 2 14-30 adapter, and the Grizzl-E Mini ships set to 40 A, so the buyer has to turn it down to 24 A.
standout_why: I read plugandrange.com/portable-chargers/nema-14-30, thechargecurve.com/home-ev-chargers/best-nema-14-30, the NeoCharge adapters help page (cited by ChatGPT) and our own dealectric.com page. Each rival covers part of this. Plug & Range has the Grizzl-E's 40 A factory default, a general warning about adapters, and the EVDANCE cable split (21.9 ft from control box to car, 3.1 ft from box to plug). The Charge Curve has the general 208 V figure (about 5 kW) and passes on NeoCharge's point that the Tesla adapter sets the current. NeoCharge has the $45 adapter price and the automatic 24 A. None of them puts these side by side as a table of how each charger stays at 24 A. No page totals the Tesla setup (connector plus a $45 adapter). Our page has none of this, and it lists the Splitvolt cable as 16.4 ft while ChatGPT showed a 26 ft Splitvolt.
decides: It supports the EVDANCE 14-30 J1772 as the pick for non-Tesla cars, because no setting goes above 24 A, so it can't draw too much from a 30 A dryer circuit. For a Tesla, the Mobile Connector with Tesla's 14-30 adapter is also limited to 24 A, but only if the buyer gets that adapter separately ($45 per NeoCharge). A 40 A charger such as the Grizzl-E Mini on a dryer outlet relies on the owner setting it to 24 A, so it should be a lower pick or carry a clear warning.
candidates: Tesla Mobile Connector + Gen 2 NEMA 14-30 adapter

findings.label: How the 24 A limit is set
findings.value: 24 A is the highest setting; the choices are 10, 16, 20 and 24 A
findings.source_title: EVDANCE Level 2 NEMA 14-30 24A J1772 Portable EV Charger | ETL Certification
findings.note: The page says 'Adjust the current limit (10A/16A/20A/24A)'. That means no setting goes over 80% of a 30 A breaker. It also says '5.76KW output', which is 24 A × 240 V. Plug & Range says another EVDANCE store page lists '6-32A' and that the manual says 24 A maximum. The page does not say what the current setting is when the charger powers up, and it links no manual.

findings.value: 5.76 kW at 240 V; 4.99 kW at 208 V
